objective: Tree-based supervised machine-learning concepts: decision trees, random forest, boosting (XGBoost), and bootstrap aggregation
secondaryObjectives: Foundational machine-learning concepts: loss functions, the bias-variance tradeoff, class-imbalance mitigations (SMOTE, oversampling), regularization, cross-validation, ensemble models, and model drift

sources.cite: CompTIA DataAI DY0-001 V1 Exam Objectives, document version 8.0: Mathematics and Statistics 17%, Modeling, Analysis and Outcomes 24%, Machine Learning 24%, Operations and Processes 22%, Specialized Applications 13%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of CompTIA's PDF. Relevant text: 'Class imbalance and mitigations' (oversampling the minority class, undersampling the majority class, SMOTE); 'Model drift causes' (data drift, concept drift); 'Explain the importance of DevOps and MLOps principles in data science' (model deployment, model performance monitoring). The objective wording here is the course seed's. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's loan-data-bias-dataai (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: single decision trees have high variance and tend to overfit, and random forests reduce variance by averaging diverse trees; bootstrap samples allow out-of-bag estimates (oob_score); gradient boosting can stop early on validation loss (early_stopping, validation_fraction, n_iter_no_change); impurity-based feature importances come from training data and favor high-cardinality features, and permutation importance does not have these flaws.

The organization, the systems, the data and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the data scientist building a loan-default model for Fairmont Credit Union, a fictional lender. The business owner wants a model and the top three drivers by Friday.
handover: 120,000 past loans with 40 features, including customer_id and branch_id.
A held-out test set is reserved for the final check.
howItWorks: The console shows the open dataset, its quality flags and a table of the checks and their results.
Move on a step at a time. A decision comes to you at each step; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

parts.label: Model
parts.criteria: Random forest, cross-validated; boosting with early stopping.
parts.modelAnswer: A single tree overfit (99% versus 71%). A random forest cross-validates at 84%; the boosted model stops at about 300 trees on validation loss.

parts.label: Drivers
parts.modelAnswer: customer_id ranked first only because impurity importance favors many-valued fields; on held-out data, debt-to-income, missed payments and loan term drive defaults.

scoring.modelReasoning: Decision trees overfit; bagging into a random forest reduces variance, measured by cross-validation with the test set kept clean. Boosting keeps fitting the training data, so stop early on validation loss. Impurity importance favors high-cardinality fields such as IDs; drop identifiers and use permutation importance on held-out data.
